title: Pakistan’s Punitive Gamble in Afghanistan: An Open War With No End in Sight
gist: Pakistan conducted air and drone strikes on ten locations in Afghanistan on Sept 24, 2026, including Kandahar where Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada is based, following earlier strikes that killed three civilians. The author frames this as a punitive gamble opening an open-ended war.

insights.claim: On September 24, 2026 Pakistan carried out air and drone strikes on ten locations inside Afghanistan, reportedly including Kandahar, the base of Taliban supreme leader Hibatullah Akhundzada, as well as Khost and Paktia.
insights.speaker: Shanthie Mariet D’Souza
insights.so_what: Striking the Taliban leadership's home province marks a major escalation in South Asian conflict risk.
insights.locator: In the early hours of September 24

insights.claim: Pakistan justified the strikes as responses to attempted attacks, claiming it had shot down ten rudimentary drones launched from Afghanistan using a 'soft kill' approach.
insights.speaker: Shanthie Mariet D’Souza
insights.so_what: Cheap drone attacks are now triggering interstate air strikes, lowering the threshold for escalation.

insights.claim: Pakistani strikes on Kunar and Paktika on September 21, 2026 killed three civilians, confirmed by UNAMA, while Islamabad claimed 28 militants killed, sparking protests in Kabul and elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Shanthie Mariet D’Souza
insights.so_what: Civilian casualties fuel Afghan nationalist backlash, making de-escalation harder.

insights.claim: The author characterizes Pakistan's punitive campaign in Afghanistan as an open war with no end in sight.
insights.speaker: Shanthie Mariet D’Souza
insights.so_what: Prolonged conflict adds to Pakistan's fiscal and security stress and regional instability.
